answer: Horizon Anchoring requires identities to maintain a continuous stake that decays slowly over time. Each identity must renew its entry fee monthly, with the cost rising proportionally to how many others claim the same horizon. This voyage mechanism forces attackers to outbid not just one but a growing pool of legitimate participants to sustain fake accounts long enough to coordinate. At any summit of activity, only those with genuine, persistent investment can remain recognized, while sybils are priced out by the escalating cost of maintaining parallel existences.
